title: Zooming out in the held world: keep the blocky stop, or skip it?
question: Walking out from close up you get crisp, crisp, BLOCKY, crisp. The blocky one is the only stop that fits the whole world top to bottom; the one after it is crisp but leaves a quarter of the screen black. Keep the blocky stop, or should zooming out jump straight from stop 2 to stop 4?
context_md:
Asked once before in my words, not yours — you answered "keep rung 3 as a soft stop" and then said you didn't know what soft stop meant. That was a fair complaint about the question. Here it is again with pictures and no jargon.

**Zooming out in the held world has four stops.** Each pane below is one press of zoom-out, in order. Every pane is shown at the same size on screen, so the only difference you are looking at is how much world you see and how crisp it is.

| stop | how much world | how it looks | empty screen |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 512 x 320 cells | crisp | none |
| 2 | 1024 x 640 | crisp | none |
| **3** | **1536 x 960 — the whole world, top to bottom** | **blocky** | **none** |
| 4 | 2048 x 1280 | crisp | **a quarter of the screen is black** |

**Why stop 3 is blocky and the others aren't:** the renderer can only draw a cell 1, 2 or 4 screen-pixels wide. Stops 2 and 4 divide evenly into that; stop 3 doesn't, so it falls back to the coarsest setting. It is not a bug and there is no cheap fix — you already looked at the version that fixes it and preferred stop 4 instead (card 20260914T000047337Z-693fcc).

**So the only question left is whether stop 3 should be on the ladder at all.** Nothing is blocked either way: keeping it is what ships today, removing it is a one-line change.

items.label: Stop 3 — the blocky one
items.caption: 1536 x 960 cells — the whole world, top to bottom. Blocky: every cell is drawn at the coarsest size.

items.label: Stop 4 — furthest
items.caption: 2048 x 1280 cells. Crisp, but the world is only 960 tall, so a quarter of the screen is black. This is the one you picked when I asked which you liked at rest.
